races.name: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Novices' Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Kenzo Des Bruyeres
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who should lead unchallenged; James Bowen rides for his father Mickey Bowen and knows this horse well, but his record on good ground in recent starts (five placings from seven sim-going runs, no wins) warrants a note of caution about his finishing effort once headed.

runners_data.name: Swingforthefence
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator who has placed once from four good-ground runs; a 50-day absence and tongue-tie headgear are relevant flags, and at 2m7f (longest trip here) his stamina is unproven beyond 2m3f in his recorded history, which is a real concern if the pace is slow and he needs to sprint.

runners_data.name: Broadway Honey
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has finished fifth three times in a row including at 2m6f on good ground, suggesting reliability without a win; at 99 days off the track this is a notable return from absence, and Sam Twiston-Davies partners a horse trained by his family, giving some confidence in the fitness preparation.

runners_data.name: Izzy's Grey
runners_data.note: Has strong place form on good ground (14 from 15 sim-going runs, three places) and is at his most dangerous when able to come from well off the pace — this race's slow tempo means he is unlikely to see out his preferred late-run scenario from wherever he settles, tempering confidence despite the course-going suitability.

runners_data.name: Jo Arengeot Bey AA
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's runner brings recent form including a win and two places at 2m4f-2m6f on good ground, and 13 days since last run suggests freshness; a natural prominent racer who should be ideally positioned tracking the leader, and Gavin Sheehan is a composed pilot for a trip like this.

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: His best efforts — two seconds from 15 good-ground starts — have come at 2m6f, so the trip suits, but his true role is as a hold-up horse and the slow pace created by a single front-runner means he may find himself unable to deliver a telling challenge from the position he ends up occupying; Bryan Carver takes over in the saddle here.

races.paceDynamic: Kenzo Des Bruyeres is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner novice handicap chase over 2m7f at Worcester, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, he should dictate a measured, uncontested gallop on good ground. Jo Arengeot Bey AA is the only genuine prominent racer and will likely slot in directly behind, meaning the early pace is controlled and the tempo unlikely to be truly punishing. The hold-up brigade — Swingforthefence, Broadway Honey, Izzy's Grey and Man Oh Man — will be tracking from varying distances off the pace, though Izzy's Grey and Man Oh Man are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map due to congestion at the rear, so their ability to secure their natural ground-saving position is not guaranteed. This race shape, with one uncontested leader and a sustainable pace, most favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles: a horse who can travel comfortably near the head of affairs will dictate their own race, leaving the hold-up runners dependent on a late collapse of the leader that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kenzo Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Kenzo Des Bruyeres leads from the front and is never seriously challenged for the lead throughout.
scenarios.body: Kenzo Des Bruyeres sets a controlled, comfortable gallop over the 2m7f trip, conserving enough energy to sustain his jumping and maintain his advantage into the straight; on good ground this suits a horse who can bowl along at his own pace without being wound up early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Jo Arengeot Bey AA tracks Kenzo Des Bruyeres throughout and overtakes in the final stages as the leader tires.
scenarios.body: Jo Arengeot Bey AA, who has a win and multiple places at this sort of trip on good ground, travels just off the pace and produces a sustained challenge from the second-last, getting the better of the weakening leader; Gavin Sheehan's experience and the horse's strong recent placing form make this a credible alternative outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run and a hold-up horse produces a telling burst from the rear.
scenarios.body: Swingforthefence or Broadway Honey would need Kenzo Des Bruyeres to go off faster than expected and weaken noticeably from the third-last, allowing a closer to reel in the leaders over the final two fences; Broadway Honey's consistent placing form at 2m7f on good ground is the most credible threat from this group, though the anticipated sedate pace makes this scenario unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Races In Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If there are significant jumping errors, falls or a dramatically altered pace scenario that reshuffles the race.
scenarios.body: Multiple incidents or a sudden collapse in the leader's jumping could open the race up to any survivor who stays jumping cleanly; the redistributed hold-up horses Izzy's Grey and Man Oh Man, racing out of their natural role, are most vulnerable to being caught in the wrong position if the race is scrambled.

watchPoints.text: Kenzo Des Bruyeres jumping — if he makes a significant error at any of the fences in the back straight, Jo Arengeot Bey AA is ideally placed to capitalise immediately and the race shape changes entirely.
Swingforthefence returning after 50 days off with tongue-tie fitted; a fitness question mark combined with an unproven stamina profile beyond 2m3f could mean he drops out suddenly in the final mile.
Broadway Honey is 99 days off the track — even with a yard that prepares horses carefully, a first-time-out run over this demanding 2m7f trip on good ground could find him short of his best fitness.

With Izzy's Grey and Man Oh Man both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield, watch whether they can even get their preferred position early — if they end up racing closer than ideal, their finishing kicks may be compromised and the race could be less competitive than the field size implies.

The overall pace is expected to be modest with only one genuine front-runner; if Kenzo Des Bruyeres bowls along at a crawl, the race may turn into a sprint from the final fence, which historically advantages horses with a prominent position rather than those coming from the rear.

races.name: FBC Manby Bowdler Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Crebilly
runners_data.note: Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill's 9yo wears a hood and is a confirmed hold-up performer, last seen winning over 20f on Good ground 21 days ago — his sim-going record (4/15 with 1W2P) is modest but his recent profile is solid, and he is the strongest genuine closer in the race if the front end folds late.|

runners_data.name: Snipe
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this Dan Skelton-trained 9yo who is a true hold-up performer by nature but has been slotted to midfield on the map due to overcrowding at the rear — 106 days off the track is a significant concern, the small five-runner field limits late-run opportunities, and despite the powerful yard being in excellent form (9/25 in 14 days), the structural disadvantages cap his probability meaningfully.|

runners_data.name: Karnaval Point
runners_data.note: David Pipe's 6yo is the sole front-runner here, twice a winner including on Good ground, and wears a hood (hg:b) which helps concentration — on a turning, jump-friendly track like Worcester, being able to dictate his own rhythm makes him dangerous, though a STYLE_FIT flag means he may not always secure the lead and should be discounted slightly if forced into a chase.|

runners_data.name: Glen To Glen
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's 4yo was a winner last time over 20f on Good ground but returns just five days later, a very quick turnaround that raises fitness and freshness questions; a hold-up performer by style, the young horse (age 4) has shown both ability and inconsistency in his record (10-5R1) and the short break combined with the small field may make it hard for him to produce his best.|

runners_data.name: Youdecide
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's 6yo arrives in hot form having won his last two outings on Good ground at 21f and 22f, making today's trip and conditions ideal; he races prominently and will likely slot in behind Karnaval Point, giving him a natural racing position that suits — the only question is whether he has enough to peg back a front-runner if the lead is not relinquished.|

races.paceDynamic: Karnaval Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with Youdecide the only other prominent-style runner, is set to dictate at a controlled, uncontested tempo on Good ground at Worcester — a track that rewards horses who can travel economically and jump well from the front. Youdecide will likely track closely in second, meaning the pace is present but not pressurised, creating a sustainable gallop that could be lethal for a horse capable of quickening off it. The trio of hold-up types — Crebilly, Snipe, and Glen To Glen — will be held off the pace, though Snipe is redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already occupied, and its true closer profile means it may not find the gaps it needs in such a small field on a turning track. This race shape — a lone front-runner dictating an honest but unforced pace with minimal early competition — squarely favours prominent-to-front types who can control and conserve energy, provided they jump accurately, while genuine hold-up horses face the challenge of making sufficient ground in a race that may not truly fall apart at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Karnaval Point Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Karnaval Point jumps cleanly from the front and Youdecide settles without applying genuine pressure, allowing a controlled solo display.
scenarios.body: Karnaval Point sets a measured, jump-by-jump gallop that suits his front-running profile, conserving enough energy to quicken on the run-in at a track where he has winning course form; a 6yo lightly handicapped and in form (-13163), he is dangerous if granted the lead on a flat, turning track in Good conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Youdecide Presses And Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Youdecide tracks Karnaval Point closely and applies enough pressure through the race to unsettle the leader, putting him under sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: Youdecide arrives at the final fences full of running having raced prominently throughout, and his recent back-to-back wins (form: 44P-11) on Good ground at similar trips suggest he has the fitness and jumping ability to capitalise if Karnaval Point is not foot-perfect; Ben Jones has been riding in form and the horse carries a career-best level of confidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and the front two runners exhaust each other, opening a late run for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Crebilly, the most natural and proven hold-up performer in the field with a recent win over today's trip on Good ground, is best placed to mop up if the race is truly run to suit closers; Glen To Glen, a lightly-raced 4yo, also has upside but has shown erratic behaviour and the short turnaround (5 days) is a concern.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Snipe Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If Snipe, held up in its natural deep-closing role, finds a cleaner run than its redistribution suggests and arrives late with a powerful finish.
scenarios.body: At OR 127 with a trainer in sharp form (Dan Skelton 9/25 over 14 days) and Harry Skelton in the plate, the talent is undeniable, but 106 days off the track, a small field on a turning track, and the redistribution all suppress this scenario meaningfully; it requires a near-perfect trip and front runners to fade genuinely.

watchPoints.text: Karnaval Point's jumping — if he makes a significant jumping error at any fence on this right-handed turning track, it could unwind his lead entirely and hand the race to Youdecide.

Glen To Glen's five-day turnaround is unusually quick and Kielan Woods may need to manage a horse who has shown an 'R' (refused/refused to race) in recent form — any temperament issue in the paddock or at the start should be noted.

Snipe's 106-day absence is the longest layoff in the field; watch closely in the pre-race and early stages to assess whether Dan Skelton has him sharp enough to produce a competitive effort first time back.

With only five runners and three genuine hold-up horses, the closing group may get too close together from the start — watch whether Crebilly and Glen To Glen interfere with each other's run and who gets a cleaner path on the run-in.

Youdecide's weight (149lbs) is the lightest in the field by a clear margin — on a flat, galloping track in Good conditions this advantage is worth monitoring if the race develops into a stamina test in the closing stages.

races.name: Step Into Luxury With Purple Granite Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
CopyBet Follow Us On X Maiden Hurdle Race (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Baltic
runners_data.note: Trainer Lucy Wadham's runner has form at up to 2m on good ground and a recent hurdles placing over course-relevant trips, but this genuine hold-up performer has been pushed into midfield by the race's congested rearward traffic — in a field this size, getting a clear run in the straight will be the real challenge rather than the pace itself.

runners_data.name: Billy Butcher
runners_data.note: Off 701 days, trainer Dave Roberts sends this eight-year-old back after a lengthy absence, and despite Lewis Saunders's 5lb claim softening the weight, his hold-up preference will leave him detached from a pace that is unlikely to be strong enough to bring him into it — the long layoff is the overriding flag here.

runners_data.name: Bluey Bay
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley's runner holds a modest record in soft ground primarily and returns after 179 days; hurdling form shows no wins and limited placed efforts in relevant conditions, and a deep hold-up style means he is dependent on a pace scenario that looks unlikely to materialise today.

runners_data.name: Emerald Tir
runners_data.note: Ryan Hatch's lightly raced five-year-old has a single hurdling run to his name — a fourth on good ground at this trip — and his unknown style profile adds genuine uncertainty; Toby McCain-Mitchell's 3lb claim is useful but the form book is too thin to read the pattern with any confidence.

runners_data.name: Lock Stock
runners_data.note: Stuart Edmunds's runner was placed twice over 2m on soft ground and once on good, suggesting the surface is not an issue, and Charlie Hammond brings experience; the 258-day absence is worth monitoring but he has the profile of a horse who could creep into this from a prominent position if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Thepassingcyclone
runners_data.note: Harry Bannister takes the ride for Dominic Ffrench Davis on the confirmed front-runner; the pace map identifies him as the controlling influence, but his form includes an unseated and two mid-pack finishes, and the STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder that his hold on the race is not bankable — if he is caught by a prominent chaser, his chance diminishes quickly.

runners_data.name: Action Replay
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden is an elite booking for Charlie Longsdon's four-year-old who has a fall on his sole hurdle run and is therefore genuinely unknown in terms of jumping profile; going is tagged UNKNOWN but the trainer's recent form (2/3 in 14 days) and Cobden's presence make this one of the more intriguing unexposed runners in the field.

runners_data.name: Arbitration
runners_data.note: Joe Tizzard's four-year-old has a strong placed record over hurdles on good ground and was runner-up twice in recent starts, with hurdle headgear now fitted; Brendan Powell steers a horse that should sit prominently and whose form line at 2m on good ground reads better than his OR of 105 suggests in what is a wide-open maiden.

runners_data.name: C'Est Pour Moi
runners_data.note: Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell's 7lb claim helps at the weights for Nigel & Willy Twiston-Davies, but three starts in good ground have produced only 6th, 7th and 9th, and a hold-up preference (headgear: p) combined with no visible improvement in form makes this a difficult proposition at a competitive OR of 120.

runners_data.name: Giant's Way
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. partners Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill's charge, a trainer with strong recent form (2/13 in 14 days); three runs on good ground showing 5th, 6th and 9th is not inspiring but the prominent style (headgear: t) suits this likely pace scenario, and a first-time headgear effect could sharpen his early response.

runners_data.name: Savanna Storm
runners_data.note: David Pipe's four-year-old (headgear: h) has shown 4th, 7th and 8th in three good-ground starts, and Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim helps offset a modest form line; a natural hold-up inclination means the expected pace scenario works against him, and there is little in the record to suggest a reversal of form.

runners_data.name: Sytadel
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton and Dan Skelton are one of the sport's most potent combinations (9/25 in 14 days), and this four-year-old holds an UNKNOWN going profile after 492 days off the track; the unexposed angle is compelling, the stable form is excellent, and Skelton's ability to produce horses first time up after a long absence cannot be discounted regardless of his unknown style tag.

runners_data.name: Teleleo
runners_data.note: Martin Keighley's four-year-old has a hurdles win and a fourth from two starts, both on good ground over this 2m trip — exactly the profile that suits today's likely race shape; Sean Bowen is a major upgrade in the saddle, and a hold-up headgear flag (h) combined with sound jumping on a flat track makes this one of the better-placed runners for the dominant scenario.

runners_data.name: Troy Story
runners_data.note: Dave Roberts's four-year-old steps up massively in trip from all-weather flat form on Tapeta/Standard ground, having never run on turf or over obstacles — there is simply no meaningful evidence for how he will handle hurdles, good ground, or 2m in this company, and a back-of-the-pack profile in flat form leaves him entirely at the mercy of circumstances.

races.paceDynamic: Thepassingcyclone is the confirmed front-runner and looks set to control this 2m maiden hurdle at a sustainable, uncontested pace on good ground at Worcester — a flat, galloping track that rewards those who travel comfortably and jump fluently. With no genuine challenger likely to push Thepassingcyclone for the lead early, the race should settle into a steady-to-honest rhythm, with Arbitration and Giant's Way likely to press from a prominent position just off the shoulder. This shape — controlled pace, not truly searching — tends to compress the race into the final two flights, making it genuinely competitive late but rewarding horses that have raced handy throughout rather than those forced wide or making up a lot of ground. The tactical verdict favours prominent racers who can sit within striking distance of the leader through the early stages and pounce from the home turn, particularly those jumping accurately enough to maintain their pitch — closers who need a true end-to-end gallop to get into the race are at a disadvantage. The field contains more hold-up types than the race map can honestly accommodate at the rear: Baltic and Billy Butcher are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield, but in a field of 14 with several others preferring to race off the pace, Teleleo and Arbitration are best placed to secure the prominent positions that will matter most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thepassingcyclone Controls, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Thepassingcyclone bowls along at a comfortable tempo and the race is won from the front two or three positions off the final bend.
scenarios.body: Thepassingcyclone sets a measured clip, giving prominent trackers a smooth, uninterrupted passage throughout, and the race is decided by who travels best into the final flight; horses that have settled just behind the leader — Teleleo, Arbitration, Giant's Way — are perfectly positioned to capitalise without ever being asked a searching question of stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and horses bunch up, compressing the race into a sprint from the third-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: A dawdling tempo can paradoxically benefit sharper, more agile types who have the tactical speed to quicken in the straight; horses with flat-race pace or good hurdling fluency who can accelerate late — Sytadel, Action Replay — may not need a searching gallop to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up, Closers Get In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more genuine than expected — perhaps through early jostling in a 14-runner field — and the race becomes truly run from halfway.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace raises the premium on horses that can conserve energy mid-race and finish strongly; Baltic, despite being mapped to midfield, is a genuine hold-up type whose form in similar good-ground conditions and ability to pick off tiring rivals late gives it an outside chance if the shape genuinely opens up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Fragments, Chaos Rules
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or interference in the early stages disrupt the field and create an unpredictable race with multiple lead changes.
scenarios.body: A fragmented race at 2m over hurdles at Worcester can produce a surprise winner whose natural boldness at the obstacles carries them clear of disorder; Emerald Tir as an unexposed unknown and Troy Story stepping up markedly in trip both carry a speculative each-way profile in this shape only.

watchPoints.text: Sytadel (Harry Skelton / Dan Skelton, 9/25 recent form, 492 days off) is a major dark horse — the stable angle alone demands respect and the unexposed profile at 2m over hurdles means he could improve dramatically on any fair estimate of his chance.

Teleleo is the best-placed runner for the dominant pace scenario: Sean Bowen's booking, two good-ground hurdling starts at this exact trip, and a win already on the board make him a significant factor in any race decided from the prominent positions.

Action Replay — Harry Cobden takes the ride on an unknown quantity with a fall on his only hurdle run; the jockey booking is significant enough to flag a potential overperformance, but jumping safety is the key watch point heading into the first flight.

Billy Butcher returns after 701 days and a hold-up style that puts him at the mercy of the pace — if the race develops genuinely, he could run on into a placed finish, but monitor his early jumping on comeback; a mistake at an early flight in a 14-runner field could end his race before it starts.

With 14 runners over 2m at Worcester, early positional jostling in the first half-mile is a real possibility — watch for crowding at the first two hurdles, particularly among the hold-up brigade (Baltic, C'Est Pour Moi, Savanna Storm) who may find themselves tighter than ideal and unable to recover ground on a track that does not offer a long straight run-in.

races.name: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Daaris
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type trained by Kevin & Lauren Frost who has been consistent at staying trips but has no wins from two placed runs on similar going; best recent form came on good 13 days ago but the step back to 2m7f hurdles and a record showing just placed efforts on comparable ground limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Crafty Gael
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the mount for Olly Murphy, whose yard is 0/10 in the past 14 days, but Crafty Gael has placed in seven of 15 runs on good ground and brings two placings over 20f on good at its last two starts; a genuine hold-up horse who should get a clean run in this configuration, stamina is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Brionywells
runners_data.note: McPherson's six-year-old has won twice at the trip on good ground and placed in four of its last five starts on good, making it statistically the best-credentialled horse in the field for this surface and distance combination; ridden by the 3lb claimer Nick Slatter, the weight relief is useful, and headgear is not fitted, suggesting a consistent jumper who travels through races well.

runners_data.name: Butchers Bill
runners_data.note: Anthony Day's six-year-old is a true hold-up horse whose recent form has been modest (falls, pulled-ups and a seventh), and having been off 100 days this is a fitness query; the horse's natural rear-running style means it is mapped into midfield by necessity, and racing in an unnatural forward position compounds what is already a doubtful profile.

runners_data.name: Forest Spirit
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen, who is 6/18 in the last 14 days, saddles this five-year-old ridden by James Bowen — a live yard angle — and Forest Spirit has placed three times from 11 runs on good going; its true instinct is to race from the rear, so finding itself pushed into midfield by the volume of hold-up types is a tactical inconvenience, though it is a young horse that may adapt.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: The one genuine front-runner in the race for Harriet Dickin, a four-year-old wearing a visor who has placed in three of ten on good ground; Megan Bevan's 7lb claim reduces the burden to 153lbs and as sole pace-setter it will face no pressure for the lead, though the horse has not won in seven starts and sustaining effort over 2m7f is the key question.

runners_data.name: Could Be You
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's six-year-old carries a ⚠ finish-fade flag and has not completed in three of its last five starts, making it among the most unreliable profiles in the field; a natural hold-up horse forced into midfield, and with only two placings in six runs on good going and zero wins, this is a difficult profile to support in any scenario.

runners_data.name: French Diablo
runners_data.note: David Bass partners Max Comley's four-year-old, which has a win and a place from four runs on good ground over 22f — directly relevant experience; as the only genuine prominent-style horse aside from Athena's Dream, it is positioned to track the leader throughout and is ideally placed to capitalise if Athena's Dream fades on the long run-in.

runners_data.name: Ramaah
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies's five-year-old returns after 67 days and has placed in three of seven runs on good going over similar trips, wearing a visor; a natural hold-up horse mapped into midfield by circumstance, the layoff is a mild concern, but the course-trip profile is solid and James Best is an experienced pilot for this type of staying race.

runners_data.name: Tis But A Scratch
runners_data.note: Georgie Howell's ten-year-old returns from a 481-day absence, which is the dominant concern regardless of other factors; a genuine hold-up type mapped into midfield by the field's composition, the horse has experience at 24f on good ground and has placed before, but asking it to be competitive first-time out after well over a year off is a significant ask, even with the 5lb pull through claiming company.

runners_data.name: Alex The Great
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll, 5/48 over the past 14 days, sends out this six-year-old who has shown no form beyond a fourth in two starts at 22f — the rest of its record comes at much shorter trips; a natural hold-up horse wearing tongue-tie and blinkers, the trip looks like new territory and the consistent middle-of-the-field finishes on flat form do not encourage.

races.paceDynamic: Athena's Dream is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m7f novices' limited handicap hurdle and, ridden by Megan Bevan, will set a sustainable gallop from the outset with no genuine rival likely to challenge for the lead — French Diablo is the only other prominent-style runner and is more likely to track than fight for the front. With the pace controlled and honest rather than frenetic on good ground over this staying trip, the race will be run at a rhythm that suits resolute travellers who can get into a position to challenge from the home turn. The redistribution in this field is significant: Butchers Bill, Forest Spirit, Could Be You, Ramaah, Tis But A Scratch and Alex The Great are all true hold-up types who cannot all slot to the rear of just 11 runners and will be pushed forward into midfield against their natural inclinations, meaning many will race out of role. This race shape — a lone front-runner at a steady clip over a staying distance on good ground — most strongly favours hold-up horses with genuine stamina and a proven record at the trip who can travel in a stalking position and produce a sustained late challenge from the home turn; Brionywells and Crafty Gael, both authentic hold-up types with solid course-distance profiles, are best placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Athena's Dream Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Athena's Dream maintains a sustainable lead unchallenged and the pace is just sufficient to string the field out without inviting a rush.
scenarios.body: Athena's Dream dictates from the front, the field settles into a long-strung procession, and the home turn arrives before closers can properly wind up their challenges; French Diablo, tracking closest, is ideally positioned to pounce if the leader weakens on the long run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If the steady gallop conserves enough energy in the chasing pack that genuine hold-up horses with stamina can deliver sustained runs from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Brionywells, with two wins at the trip on good ground and the form to finish strongly, and Crafty Gael, who has placed in four of nine on similar going, are best placed to reel in tying leaders late; the long Worcester straight rewards those who travel smoothly through the race and peak on the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Held-Up Winners
scenarios.trigger: If the modest gallop set by Athena's Dream causes a bunched finish and multiple horses sprint from the same point, favouring those with residual toe.
scenarios.body: This scenario relies heavily on redistributed hold-up types — Butchers Bill, Forest Spirit, Could Be You — racing in unnatural midfield positions and producing turn-of-foot, which is structurally less likely given most are stamina types; if it does materialise, Forest Spirit's recent placed form and James Bowen's course knowledge give it the best claim among the out-of-role contingent.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chaos, Surprise Result
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fatigue, or the longer 2m7f trip catches out several hold-up horses racing out of position and the field splinters across the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Could Be You's inconsistent jumping record and the large cluster of genuinely stamina-untested horses suggest attrition is a live outsider risk; a horse like Tis But A Scratch, experienced over this trip on good ground despite a long absence, could emerge from chaos, though the 481-day break makes this a fragile case.

watchPoints.text: Watch Athena's Dream's jumping closely from the third-last — if the front-runner starts to fidget or fiddles a hurdle on the home turn, French Diablo has the momentum to go past immediately and the race could be decided in a single stride.

Brionywells is the most statistically reliable horse for this course-distance-going combination with two wins and three places in nine relevant starts; if Nick Slatter gets it into a smooth rhythm behind the pace, a sustained challenge from the second-last is the danger move in the race.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Butchers Bill, Forest Spirit, Could Be You, Ramaah, Tis But A Scratch, Alex The Great — all forced into midfield creates congestion from the first hurdle; watch for crowding, shuffling, and potential jumping interference on the tight Worcester bends in the opening mile.

Could Be You's finishing-fade flag and three non-completions in five runs make it a significant risk as a loose horse or faller; with 11 runners over 2m7f, one jumping incident could disrupt the entire chasing pack and change the shape of the race entirely.

Forest Spirit's trainer Mickey Bowen is running at a 33% strike rate over the past 14 days (6/18), a significant yard angle worth noting — if James Bowen settles it comfortably off the pace in its natural style despite the redistribution pressure, it may outrun its position in the market.

races.name: CopyBet BOG Now For Doncaster Tomorrow Handicap Hurdle Race (Div I)

runners_data.name: Flawless Clarity
runners_data.note: The confirmed leader here and racing back after 340 days off, which is the single biggest question mark — she has Good-ground form (3/4 in similar conditions) and the style to control this from the front, but a near-year absence for a seven-year-old makes fitness and jumping sharpness genuinely uncertain.

runners_data.name: Getaway With You
runners_data.note: Trainer McPherson has had 1 winner from 4 in the last 14 days and this prominent-style racer arrives 144 days fresh; tongue-tie fitted, and while Good-ground figures are modest (3/15, no win, no place), he stays the trip and could organically take up second behind Flawless Clarity.

runners_data.name: Sweet Honey B
runners_data.note: Ran just 22 days ago and has a clear preference for Soft ground (all her placed efforts on give), so the Good surface here is a genuine worry; hold-up style means she needs the pace to stretch, and the controlled gallop expected does not suit.

runners_data.name: Jessie Jump Jet
runners_data.note: Classy hold-up performer with a strong record on Good ground (9/13, five placed efforts) and consistently close-up at the finish; blinkered, which adds an attention element, and her trainer fires at 1/1 in the past 14 days — if anyone bridges the gap from hold-up to stalker today, it is her.

runners_data.name: Berry Edge
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton is a powerful yard-jockey combination, and Berry Edge returns after 177 days with her recent form entirely on Soft/Heavy; the step back to Good ground is an unknown, though she won on Soft and trips at 16f suit better than this 2m4f.

runners_data.name: Harry Gulliver
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 20f and brings recent course experience (13 days ago), though his results are inconsistent (form 138/56); a genuine closer by nature who has been placed into the midfield map because of the surplus of hold-up horses — his actual tactical preference is to race from the rear, so he may end up further back than the map suggests.

runners_data.name: Sweet Serene
runners_data.note: Won on Soft at 18f and her last visit to Good ground produced a 12th-of-12 at 24f — the combination of firmer going and this longer trip is concerning; by nature a hold-up type whose best form comes with cut in the ground, and the race shape here does not play to her strengths.

runners_data.name: At Sunrise
runners_data.note: A five-year-old lightly raced hurdler who pulled up on his only Soft run and sits at a modest OR of 75; his hold-up style means he relies on a fast-run race that is unlikely to materialise here, and the 103-day absence adds another layer of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Noble Recall
runners_data.note: Has a consistent placed record on Good ground (1W, 3P in 13 runs) and stays 20f well; a natural hold-up horse whose true position will likely be at the rear rather than mid-division — bumped to midfield on the map because of the crowd of closers, but in running he may be one of the most capable of making a late charge.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Spirit
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who is flagged for fading in finishes, which is a fundamental handicap in a 2m4f race that will test stamina even at a moderate gallop; has been tailed off or well beaten in all recent starts on Good ground, and the amateur rider (7lb claimer) adds further risk.

races.paceDynamic: Flawless Clarity is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 2m4f handicap hurdle, and with no natural challenger for the lead, she is set to bowl along at a controlled, unhurried gallop on Good ground at Worcester. The pace she generates will be sustainable rather than searching, meaning the race will not truly test stamina but will instead set up a finish where tactical speed and jumping fluency at the business end matter most. This scenario strongly favours prominent racers who can track Flawless Clarity comfortably and pounce from a close position when the tempo lifts in the final circuit — classic prominent-to-front profile is the beneficiary. This field is heavily stacked with genuine hold-up horses: Harry Gulliver, Sweet Serene, At Sunrise, Noble Recall and Cosmic Spirit are all true closers redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many hold-up types to occupy the rear; of those, Harry Gulliver and Noble Recall are most likely to secure a genuinely tracking position, while the others may find themselves shuffled back further than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Flawless Clarity Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Flawless Clarity bowls along uncontested, dictating a honest but not brutal tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She settles into a rhythm at the head of affairs and, with no rival pressing her, arrives at the final hurdle with reserves intact, making it very difficult for hold-up horses to reel her in. Prominent horses who track her at close range are best placed to capitalise if she tires, but she may simply have too much in the tank.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If Getaway With You or Jessie Jump Jet press Flawless Clarity more aggressively than anticipated and the pace lifts noticeably from halfway.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop from the front produces a genuine test of stamina over 2m4f Good ground, opening the door for the most relentless stayer tracking in second or third.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile and the field bunches, giving true closers a sprint-finish opportunity.
scenarios.body: A slow-motion race paradoxically can suit a fresh, well-handicapped closer if the bunching creates a messy finish with fallers or interference; Harry Gulliver and Noble Recall are the most likely beneficiaries given their genuine hold-up profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Pace Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Flawless Clarity's long absence (340 days) causes her to fire too early or make errors, triggering mid-race reshuffling.
scenarios.body: A disrupted lead sees several horses forced to adjust their position mid-race on the final bend, favouring the most adaptable jumper with residual class; Berry Edge under Harry Skelton is best equipped to capitalise on chaos.

watchPoints.text: Flawless Clarity's jumping sharpness after 340 days off is the pivotal factor — if she makes errors at early hurdles the entire race shape unravels and mid-race chaos favours Berry Edge and Getaway With You.

Harry Gulliver and Noble Recall are genuine hold-up types who the map shows in midfield but who may drift to the rear in running — punters should not assume they will be travelling in a favourable position at the turn for home.

Jessie Jump Jet's blinkers are applied in a race where she is trying to make ground from hold-up; a fresh attitude could see her race more prominently than usual and put unexpected pressure on Flawless Clarity's lead.

Berry Edge's switch from consistent Soft/Heavy ground to Good at Worcester is worth monitoring in the early stages — Harry Skelton will know quickly whether she is handling it and may adjust tactics accordingly.

The absence of a genuine pacemaker to challenge Flawless Clarity means the early gallop is likely to be deceptively slow — jockeys on hold-up horses should be watched for signs of anxiety, as early position moves in a slowly-run race can backfire badly over this trip.

races.name: CopyBet Bog Now For Doncaster Tomorrow Handicap Hurdle Race (Div II)

runners_data.name: Bathara
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. rides a horse with strong form on good ground (three placings from six similar-going runs including a win), coming into this off a lengthy 113-day break; a natural hold-up type who will need a clear run from the rear to land his late punch over this 2m4f trip.

runners_data.name: American Empire
runners_data.note: Multiple third-place finishes on good ground suggest consistency without a turn of foot; Donald McCain's runner carries a visor, has been seen just 13 days ago suggesting freshness, but the hold-up style in a race likely to be steadily run makes it hard to close the gap.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner and the key pace-setter — Charlie Longsdon's horse can control this race from flag to finish with Bass in the saddle; form figures of 3-3-P-3-5 show he places without always winning, but uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage today.

runners_data.name: Traveling Soldier
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over on a hold-up specialist with all five recent runs over this 2m4f (20f) trip and solid good-ground record; headgear (visor) applied again, and a 50-day break is not concerning for Olly Murphy, but the horse has been winless across seven similar-going runs.

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with no win from seven good-ground runs; a genuine hold-up horse pushed into mapped midfield because the rear is congested — its best chance relies on finding a gap that may not materialise, and the style-fit penalty (0.92) reflects that it is unlikely to operate in its ideal position.

runners_data.name: Farhh Echo
runners_data.note: A consistent finisher toward the back of fields on good ground with a fade-in-finish flag that compounds the redistribution issue — D J Jeffreys' runner is shown in midfield but is truly a hold-up type, and with a tendency to weaken late, this race shape offers little help.

runners_data.name: Dynamite Defense
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' five-year-old posted a third 22 days ago and has placed on good ground before; mapped to midfield but genuinely wants to race from the rear, and the style dislocation (STYLE_FIT 0.92) means it will likely never find its natural rhythm in this shape.

runners_data.name: Babychino
runners_data.note: The one prominent runner aside from Ikigai Star — Fern O'Brien (5lb claim) can slot in just behind the leader and represents the main danger if Ikigai Star fades; recent form includes a second and a third, and good-ground record (six runs, two placings) is solid enough for a young four-year-old.

runners_data.name: Inca
runners_data.note: Sophie Leech's eight-year-old has the lowest OR in the field at 71 and a 100-day absence; a true hold-up horse displaced to midfield on the map, with no wins from six good-ground runs and modest finishing positions throughout recent history — the layoff and style mismatch combine to make this an outsider's outsider.

races.paceDynamic: Ikigai Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 2m4f handicap hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, David Bass can dictate a controlled, pressure-free tempo across the good ground at Worcester. The pace will be honest but not scorching — a sustainable gallop that keeps the race together until the final turn, where Ikigai Star will aim to stretch clear before the last. Bathara, American Empire, and Traveling Soldier are natural hold-up horses who will track from the rear, while Babychino provides the only realistic prominent presence to push forward behind the leader. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Usyk, Farhh Echo, Dynamite Defense, and Inca are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, with Babychino and Traveling Soldier most likely to actually press into their natural positions behind Ikigai Star. This race shape strongly favours a prominent racer or a single closer with a powerful late surge, but above all it rewards the controlled front-runner given the absence of any serious pace pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ikigai Star Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ikigai Star is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a controlled pace that burns off hold-up horses in the straight.
scenarios.body: Bass dictates every yard, arriving at the last with a lead and enough petrol to hold on as the closers arrive too late on good ground that doesn't maximise their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Ikigai Star is slightly too quick and the hold-up horses get a genuine run at the leaders from two out.
scenarios.body: A genuinely run race wears down Ikigai Star late, and a horse with a clean passage from off the pace picks up strongly on the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Babychino or Traveling Soldier tracks Ikigai Star closely and challenges from the last hurdle, capitalising on a faltering leader.
scenarios.body: The early pace proves just enough to drain Ikigai Star in the closing stages, handing victory to the horse who conserved energy whilst still racing prominently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed midfield hold-up horses — Usyk, Dynamite Defense, or Inca — find clear runs and produce a finishing effort from their unnatural positions.
scenarios.body: Racing out of role reduces their chance materially, but a well-timed run from one of the lower-rated hold-up types catches a fading field late; the style mismatch and OR disadvantage makes this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Ikigai Star — if David Bass gets a soft lead unchallenged, the entire field is chasing a horse who could control the tempo entirely; watch whether anything attempts to go with him in the first mile.

Babychino — the only genuine prominent runner behind Ikigai Star; if Fern O'Brien (5lb claimer) can slot in second and Ikigai Star weakens late, Babychino is best-placed structurally to inherit the lead at the last.

Bathara — the 113-day absence combined with Jonjo O'Neill Jr. in the saddle makes this interesting; if the hold-up closers get any sort of run with two to jump, Bathara's good-ground form and trip suitability make it the most dangerous of the rear group.

Usyk, Dynamite Defense, Inca, and Farhh Echo — four hold-up horses all competing for the same limited closing ground; watch for traffic issues from two out if any of them produce a run simultaneously through a narrow gap.
